title: USO show personnel and three months of rehearsal
summary: He names the reeds, brass, rhythm and singers, and says the timed show could not be changed and was rehearsed for three months.

blocks.x: Now, the USO show personnel.
Yeah. Now, I'll give you the reed section first. There was myself first -- I get to be at the top of the list.
Did you take along a clarinet, or just the alto?
Holmes (12/5) - 8
No, just the alto. And there was Franz Jackson on tenor saxophone. And Dave McRae, who played alto and baritone saxophone. In fact, he could play them all. He played clarinet.
Didn't Jackson double?
He could play clarinet, but he didn't do any clarinet playing. Dave McRae played the clarinet.
Any doubling that was done by the reeds, he did.

Yeah, McRae did it. Then in the brass section was Louis Bacon, trumpet, Nelson Williams, trumpet - - and I think that was all. I don't think there was a trombone. Then there was Jesse Stone on piano...
Did Stone do any arranging?
Not after the show had started. He didn't change anything. When the show opened up, that was the way it went for the entire engagement. And Teddy was the drummer's name, a fellow from Brooklyn.
And then you had a bass player.
Elwood Reynolds was the bass player. And then we had three girls. Two of them danced together, and the other girl was a vocalist, Gwen Tines(?).
Gwendolyn...?
Tines. She was from some place up in Canada. She was Canadian, but she made the trip with us.
Holmes (12/5) - 9
Sylvester Lewis was the manager.
Sylvester Lewis was the manager. He didn't play in the band, but he was a former trumpet player.
So now, you're all assembled in New York and rehearsed, got the show together...
We rehearsed for three months during the day, we got the show together, and after we got it together, then not a note was to be changed. We couldn't change any numbers in the show if we wanted to.
